submission.justification: Module-D2 at 30% wall coverage achieves the highest light collection (39.3 PE/MeV) among designs that meet the robustness requirement. Module-D1, despite having good optical performance, fails thermal cycling tests with 30% failure rate (requirement: ≤5%). Module-D2 passes with only 2% failure rate and, when operated at maximum allowed coverage (30%), delivers light collection that exceeds even Module-D1 at 20% coverage. Module-D3, while most robust (0.5% failure), achieves only 23.5 PE/MeV at 30% coverage. The chosen configuration maximizes light collection within all constraints.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three designs listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Module-D2 (wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout) is listed in candidate_specs.md

requirements.requirement: Modules must be robust, since they are inaccessible after the cryostat is filled
requirements.evidence: Module-D2 has 2% failure rate in thermal cycling tests, meeting the ≤5% requirement stated in thermal_cycling_tests.md
Recommended coverage is 30%, which is at the upper allowed limit and supported by available feedthroughs per meeting_notes_2026-01-20.md

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible light collection (photoelectrons per MeV)
requirements.evidence: Simulation shows Module-D2 at 30% coverage achieves 39.3 PE/MeV, the highest among robust designs. Module-D1 is disqualified due to 30% failure rate.
